entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Wen Tingyun, a Chinese poet born Wen Qi, courtesy name Feiqing, was a prominent lyricist of the late Tang dynasty.

He was born during the reign of Emperor Muzong of Tang (825–827 CE) and died in 870 CE, during the reign of Emperor Zhaozong of Tang (874–888 CE).

Wen Tingyun's poetry was known for its elegance and refinement, and he was often compared to other famous poets of the Tang dynasty, such as Du Fu and Li Bai.

His works include the 'Collection of Poems by Wen Tingyun', which is considered a classic of Chinese poetry.

Wen Tingyun's legacy continues to be celebrated in modern times, with his poetry still widely studied and admired in China and other countries.

In a striking quote, Wen Tingyun wrote, 'The best way to gain a friend is to be a good friend.'

Wen Tingyun's impact on Chinese literature and culture is undeniable, making him one of the most important poets of the Tang dynasty.
